extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary XML/PDF locators; automated placeholder mechanism_context_pending_review claims were replaced with bounded evidence classes.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide 35409-1 damages the E. coli ATCC 25922 cell surface and is associated with leakage of cellular contents in SEM imaging.
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports membrane/cell-envelope damage morphology but does not by itself define a molecular pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide 35409-1 permeabilizes E. coli ML35 internal membrane in an ONPG beta-galactosidase assay at 1x MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct permeabilization readout is phenotype-level; exact molecular target remains bounded to membrane permeabilization.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Serial subculture at 0.5x MIC produced a lower MIC fold-change for 35409-1 than conventional antibiotic comparators over the 18-day assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Resistance-development assay is not a direct molecular mechanism; it is preserved as phenotypic context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra and helical wheel/hydrophobic-moment analyses provide structural context for membrane selectivity hypotheses.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural predictions/context support interpretation but are not treated as direct antimicrobial mechanism evidence.

limitations: No molecular pore model is promoted beyond the SEM and ONPG permeabilization evidence.
Resistance-passaging data are treated as phenotypic context, not a direct mechanism.
